clue.text: American sailor circling shore, by the way

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so one part wraps around the other

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American
to shore up a wall is to prop it
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A US sailor walks round the coastline, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Shore is the verb, as in shoring up a building, not the coastline.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos, used as an aside, introduces an incidental remark, just as the phrase does when changing topic.

clue.text: Little girl following Jack's elder sister

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the girl's name is placed second

blocks.note: jack is slang for a sailor, as is AB, able seaman
Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A small girl trails after Jack's big sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the girl's name after the sailor; 'elder sister' reads as a sibling but means a senior nun.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess heads a convent, so she is a senior religious sister among the nuns.

clue.text: Thugs picked up Elizabethan fashion items

indicators.note: picking up a signal means hearing it, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: ruffs were the pleated collars of Tudor dress

explanation.surface: Hooligans grabbed some Tudor-era clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is an old-fashioned word for a violent ruffian or hooligan.

clue.text: Tendency to be nosy about uninhibited model

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the others

blocks.note: to pry is to be inquisitive
open means frank and unreserved
to sit for an artist is to model

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to snoop on a model who lacks inhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A propensity is a natural inclination or leaning towards some behaviour.

clue.text: Clean vessel boarded by new leader

indicators.note: a vessel boarded by someone has them inside it

blocks.note: short for submarine
Carolus Rex, the cipher of King Charles III, who acceded in 2022

explanation.surface: A newly installed leader climbs aboard a freshly cleaned ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles III became king in 2022, so CR (Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles) was the new head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub is to clean something by rubbing it hard with a brush.

clue.text: Drunken rugby player, mostly stylishly dressed

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a back is a rugby position behind the forwards
chic means elegantly fashionable

explanation.surface: A smartly turned-out rugby player is the worse for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacchus was the Roman god of wine, hence the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchic describes riotous revelry in the style of the wine god's followers, so it is a literary synonym for intoxicated.

clue.text: Economist who wrote a report the night before cracking game

indicators.note: cracking something opens it up with the other piece driven inside

blocks.note: bridge is a card game
the eve is the evening before an event

explanation.surface: An economist finished a report late the night before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: William Beveridge's 1942 report laid the foundations of Britain's welfare state.
explanation.definitionFit: William Beveridge was the British economist whose wartime report led to the welfare state and the NHS.

clue.text: Some meat sandwiches left for a bunch of zealots

indicators.note: a sandwich holds its filling, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a cut is a piece of meat from a butcher
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Fanatics are left a few meat sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' suggests a hidden word, but the meat is a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A cult is a group of devoted, often fanatical followers of a person or belief.

clue.text: What a day! To start with, this guy made a beastly noise

blocks.note: he refers to a man
eh is an exclamation asking 'what?'
taken as written
short for Wednesday

explanation.surface: After an exhausting day, a man starts braying like a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To start with' puts the man first; 'What a day!' reads as exasperation but splits into three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw imitates a donkey's bray, and a donkey is a beast of burden.

clue.text: Perhaps islander's reason for not staging play

blocks.note: first meaning: a shipwrecked person stranded on an island
second meaning: read as two words, the actors have been sent off, so no performance

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits into two words, the company of actors having been dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwreck survivor stranded on a desert island is the classic marooned figure, so an islander is one example.

clue.text: Old pugilist from Britain and a figure from Spain

blocks.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain or British
uno is Spanish for the number one

explanation.surface: A retired boxer who came from Britain, and a numeral from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Bruno was a popular British heavyweight boxer of the 1980s and 90s.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Bruno is a former heavyweight boxing champion, an example of a retired fighter.

clue.text: People in a party of left-wing English radicals initially switching sides

indicators.note: the first letter swaps from one side to the other, the left-hand abbreviation exchanged for the right-hand one

blocks.note: the Levellers were a radical egalitarian movement of the English Civil War era
L for left is replaced by R for right

explanation.surface: Members of a left-wing radical group start defecting to the other side.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levellers were 1640s English radicals demanding equal rights; swap their opening L (left) for R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Revellers are merrymakers, the sort of guests found celebrating at a festive gathering.

clue.text: Expressionist composer's chosen new pupil of his

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
Alban Berg studied under the composer being defined

explanation.surface: A modernist composer picks out a fresh student of his own.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Schoenberg taught Alban Berg and Anton Webern in Vienna.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoenberg, pioneer of atonal and twelve-tone music, is the leading musical figure of the Expressionist movement.

clue.text: Case of tequila? Cheers and cheerio!

indicators.note: a case is the outer shell, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: first and last letters of tequila
ta and cheers are both informal British ways to say thanks

explanation.surface: Someone toasts a crate of tequila and then heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' looks like a toast but means thanks; both it and the definition are casual British farewells or thank-yous.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is a chatty British goodbye, exactly the same register as the informal farewell in the clue.

clue.text: Drink from top composer not finishing round

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so the composer's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: a cap is a lid or top
Giacomo Puccini, Italian opera composer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A leading composer abandons a round of drinks before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cappuccino is an Italian coffee made with espresso and frothed milk.

clue.text: It detects law-breaking beer fans, full of energy on drug

indicators.note: to be full of something is to have it inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British beer drinkers' group
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Drunken, drugged-up beer lovers break the law and get spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMRA, the Campaign for Real Ale, is a British consumer group of real-ale enthusiasts; 'on' places the drug first.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside camera photographs cars exceeding the limit, so it catches motorists committing an offence.

clue.text: Mythic figures from Greece need muse, I suspect

indicators.note: a suspect account is dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A writer of Greek myth suspects they need inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I suspect' reads as a hedge, but 'I' belongs with the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides, 'kindly ones', is a euphemistic name for the Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek mythology.

clue.text: Waste shilling on a pair of queens?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for the old shilling
QU and ER are both abbreviations for queen, joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: Someone blows a shilling betting on two queens at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin. 'A pair of queens' reads literally as one queen 'and' another.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander money is to waste it recklessly.

clue.text: Gallons swallowed in George's house — might this result?

indicators.note: something swallowed ends up inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: G is short for gallons
the Hanoverians were the royal house of the four King Georges

explanation.surface: If someone downs gallons at George's place, what follows the next morning?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on the surface: gallons of drink swallowed lead to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the headache and nausea that follow heavy drinking, the consequence the clue predicts.

clue.text: Fashion designer with winning clothing male modelled in advance

indicators.note: to model is to shape anew, so the word just before it is reshaped
clothing someone wraps them up, so one piece dresses the other

blocks.note: Mary Quant, designer famous for the miniskirt
to be up is to be ahead in a game
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A couturier, ahead in the game, dresses a male model in advance of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Mary Quant was the British designer who popularised the miniskirt in 1960s London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic breakthrough or sudden great step forward is called a big jump, borrowing the physics term.

clue.text: Asian leader toppled Asian leader? Commotion follows!

indicators.note: a toppled figure is upended, so in a down clue the name is read bottom to top

blocks.note: Kim Jong-un, leader of North Korea
ado is fuss or bustle

explanation.surface: An Asian ruler has been overthrown, and uproar follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The same two words serve twice: a North Korean leader in the wordplay, a Japanese one as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado is a historic title for the Emperor of Japan, an East Asian ruler.

clue.text: A European supplier of oil needing treatment

blocks.note: un is French for a
an oil well supplies oil

explanation.surface: A European oil supplier is in need of processing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A European' means the word for 'a' in a European language.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwell is sick, so they require medical attention.

clue.text: Ship — and what one may carry leaving Cuba's capital

indicators.note: when something leaves it is no longer there, so that letter is taken out
'capital' keeps only the first letter of 'Cuba'

blocks.note: a ship carries freight
the capital, or first letter, of Cuba

explanation.surface: A vessel and its load depart from Havana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like Havana but is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the vessel in which Jason and the Argonauts sailed to find the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Home rule divides party giving offence

indicators.note: dividing something splits it apart with the other piece wedged in the gap

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
a faction is a party or group within a larger body
R is an abbreviation for rule

explanation.surface: Irish Home Rule splits a political party and causes offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home rule' reads as the Irish self-government cause but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a breach of a rule or law, i.e. a violation or misdemeanour.

clue.text: Liar shocked about year one's spent in Doha

indicators.note: a shock jolts things out of place, so the word's letters are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled word goes round the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
Y is short for year

explanation.surface: A liar is stunned at how long a year has been spent in Qatar.
explanation.definitionFit: The riyal is the currency of Qatar, whose capital is Doha, so it is money spent there.

clue.text: Discharging debts, inclined to work for boss

indicators.note: discharging something lets it go, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt
studious means given to study

explanation.surface: Paying off debts, someone who is keen to work for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as an employer but is the raised knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob or stud, as on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Democrat cast a ballot in English city with loyalty

indicators.note: placed in a city means set inside its name

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
to vote is to cast a ballot

explanation.surface: A Democratic supporter faithfully votes while living in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely, a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something devotedly is to do it faithfully, out of steadfast loyalty.

clue.text: Some shenanigans turning silly

indicators.note: only some of the following word is used, a run of its letters
turning round means the run of letters is read the other way

blocks.note: letters three to seven of the word

explanation.surface: A bit of mischief is becoming foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means senseless or pointless, a near synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Colour's maintained on huge screen

indicators.note: to be maintained is to be held or supported, so one piece is held inside the others

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
red is a colour; the 's stands for 'is'
OS is short for outsize

explanation.surface: Colour is kept up on an enormous cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Colour's means 'colour is', so the colour is held between the pieces from 'on' and 'huge'; 'screen' looks like a cinema screen but is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental partition or panel behind a church altar.

clue.text: Item destined for bathroom old men put in lounge

indicators.note: putting things in something places them inside it

blocks.note: to loll is to lounge lazily
O is the abbreviation for old
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Old men are sent from the lounge to the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lounge' looks like a room alongside the bathroom but is the verb. LOO is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilet paper on a cardboard tube is kept in the lavatory, so its purpose is the bathroom.
